Glossary

116 training terms explained

116 terms

A

Achilles Tendinitis

Inflammation or degeneration of the Achilles tendon causing pain at the back of the heel.

Active Recovery

Light post-exercise activity to promote metabolic waste elimination.

Z1
ACWRAcute:Chronic Workload Ratio

Ratio between recent and habitual training load, injury risk indicator.

Adaptation

Process by which the body becomes more capable through training.

Aerobic Capacity

Ability to produce energy via the aerobic system using oxygen.

Z2
Aerobic Threshold

First lactate increase above resting values.

Anabolic Window

Post-exercise period (30-60 min) when the body is most receptive to recovery nutrients.

Anaerobic Capacity

Capacity to produce energy without oxygen for short maximal efforts.

Z6
ATLAcute Training Load

Acute training load, represents recent fatigue.

B

Base Building

Phase building fundamental endurance and aerobic capacity.

Z2
BCAABranched-Chain Amino Acids

Branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) often used as supplements, but of limited use with adequate protein intake.

Black Toenail

Subungual hematoma caused by repeated impact of the toe against the shoe.

Blister

Fluid-filled pocket under the skin caused by friction between foot and shoe.

Block Periodization

Focusing efforts on specific qualities through successive blocks.

Brick Workout

Back-to-back two-discipline workout without rest, typical in triathlon.

C

Cadence

Steps per minute when running, or pedal revolutions per minute when cycling.

Caffeine

Legal ergogenic aid that improves endurance performance by 2-4%.

Capillarization

Density of small blood vessels supplying muscles.

Carbo-Loading

Strategy of increasing carbohydrate intake before a long race to maximize glycogen stores.

Compartment Syndrome

Increased pressure within a muscle compartment causing pain and tightness during exercise.

Compression

Compressive garments or devices to improve recovery.

CSSCritical Swim Speed

Critical swimming speed, the swimming equivalent of lactate threshold.

CTLChronic Training Load

Chronic training load, represents long-term fitness.

CVCritical Velocity

Maximum sustainable speed without continuous fatigue accumulation, boundary between heavy and severe exercise domains.

Z4

D

Deload Week

Recovery week with reduced training load.

DOMSDelayed Onset Muscle Soreness

Muscle soreness appearing 24-72 hours after exercise.

E

Electrolytes

Minerals (sodium, potassium, magnesium) lost in sweat, essential for muscle function.

Energy Gels

Concentrated carbohydrate supplements taken during long efforts to maintain energy.

F

Fartlek

Speed play with unstructured pace variations.

FC MaxMaximum Heart Rate

Maximum number of heartbeats per minute achievable.

FC ReposResting Heart Rate

Number of heartbeats per minute at complete rest.

Flight Phase

Period when both feet are off the ground (~60% of the gait cycle).

Foam Rolling

Self-massage with roller to release muscle tension.

Forefoot Strike

Foot strike where the ball of the foot (metatarsals) contacts the ground first.

FTPFunctional Threshold Power

Maximum power sustainable for approximately one hour in cycling.

Z4
Functional Overreaching

Planned temporary fatigue leading to supercompensation after rest.

Fundamental Endurance

Base of aerobic training, easy pace sustainable for long periods.

Z2

G

Glucose-Fructose Ratio

Optimal proportion of glucose and fructose in sports drinks to maximize carbohydrate absorption.

Glycemic Index (GI)

Scale (0-100) measuring how quickly a food raises blood sugar.

Glycogen

Stored form of glucose in muscles and liver, the primary fuel for exercise.

Ground Contact Time

Duration the foot spends on the ground with each stride.

H

Half Marathon

21.1 km race, excellent compromise between speed and endurance.

Heel Strike

Foot strike pattern where the heel contacts the ground first.

Hill Repeats

Hill repetitions to develop strength and power.

Z5
Hitting the Wall (Bonking)

Sudden onset of fatigue caused by glycogen depletion, typically around km 30.

HRVHeart Rate Variability

Variability in time between heartbeats, indicator of recovery status.

Hydration

Maintaining fluid balance before, during, and after exercise to preserve performance.

I

IFIntensity Factor

Ratio between normalized power and FTP.

Iliotibial Band Syndrome

Pain on the outer side of the knee caused by friction of the iliotibial band.

Intervals

Alternating intense efforts and recoveries to develop VO2max.

Z5
Isotonic Drink

Drink with a particle concentration close to blood, optimizing fluid absorption.

L

Lactate Threshold

Maximum intensity where lactate remains stable, limit of prolonged endurance.

Z4
Lactate Threshold

Intensity where lactate starts accumulating faster than it is cleared.

Z4
Long Run

Extended run developing endurance and aerobic adaptations.

Z2

M

Macrocycle

Long-term planning period, typically a complete season.

Maltodextrin

Rapidly absorbed glucose polymer, the main ingredient in sports drinks and gels.

Marathon

42.195 km race, the flagship endurance event in running.

Mesocycle

3-6 week training block with a specific objective.

Microcycle

Typical training week with planned sessions.

Midfoot Strike

Flat foot landing, neither heel nor forefoot first.

Mitochondria

Energy powerhouses of cells, producing ATP through oxidation.

Muscle Cramp

Sudden involuntary muscle contraction during or after exercise.

Muscle Fiber Types

Slow-twitch (type I) vs fast-twitch (type II), determining abilities.

N

Negative Split

Strategy where the second half is run faster than the first.

Non-Functional Overreaching

Excessive fatigue requiring several weeks of recovery.

NPNormalized Power

Normalized power accounting for effort variability.

O

Over-Unders

Intervals alternating just above and below threshold.

Z4
Overtraining Syndrome

Chronic fatigue state due to prolonged imbalance between load and recovery.

P

Peaking

Final preparation phase targeting maximum performance on race day.

Plantar Fasciitis

Inflammation of the plantar fascia causing sharp heel pain, especially in the morning.

Polarized Training

80/20 distribution: lots of easy volume, little high intensity, avoiding the middle.

Power-to-Weight Ratio

Ratio between power output and body weight, key for climbing.

Progressive Long Run

Long run with acceleration towards marathon pace at the end.

Z2
Progressive Overload

Principle of gradual training stress increase to progress.

Progressive Run

Run with gradual pace increase from start to finish.

Pronation

Natural inward roll of the foot after ground contact.

Pyramid Workout

Intervals with increasing then decreasing duration (or vice versa).

Z5

R

Race Pace

Training at target race-specific pace.

Recovery Proteins

Post-exercise protein intake to support muscle repair and adaptation.

Recovery Run

Very slow jog to promote active recovery.

Z1
RPERate of Perceived Exertion

Subjective effort perception scale from 1 to 10.

Runner's Iron (Iron Deficiency)

Increased iron needs in runners, with deficiency risk impacting performance.

Runner's Knee

Dull ache around or behind the kneecap, worsened by stairs and prolonged sitting.

Running Economy

Energy efficiency at a given speed, less O2 = better economy.

Running Gait Cycle

Complete cycle from one foot contact to the next contact of the same foot.

S

Shin Splints

Pain along the inner shinbone caused by repetitive stress on the bone and connective tissues.

Shoe Drop

Height difference in mm between the heel and forefoot of the shoe.

Sodium

Primary electrolyte in sweat, essential for fluid retention and muscle function.

Sprint

Very short maximal effort developing neuromuscular power.

Z6
Stance Phase

Period when the foot is in contact with the ground (~40% of the gait cycle).

Stress Fracture

Tiny bone crack caused by repetitive impacts, requiring several weeks of complète rest.

Stride Length

Distance covered per stride, determined by speed and body proportions.

Strides

Short, fluid accelerations to work on technique and speed.

Supercompensation

Adaptation phenomenon where the body becomes stronger after recovering from stress.

Supination

Outward roll of the foot (underpronation), less common.

Surge

Brief, sharp acceleration inserted within a continuous effort, typically 20-40 seconds.

Z5
Sweet Spot

Intensity zone just below threshold, offering excellent effort-to-benefit ratio.

Z3

T

Taper

Progressive volume reduction before competition to arrive fresh.

Tempo Run

Sustained run at a 'comfortably hard' pace near aerobic threshold.

Z3
Threshold

Lactate threshold work, maximum sustainable pace for 45-60 minutes.

Z4
Training Zones

Intensity classification system based on heart rate or pace.

TRIMPTraining Impulse

Training load quantification method based on heart rate.

TSBTraining Stress Balance

Difference between fitness (CTL) and fatigue (ATL), indicates freshness.

TSSTraining Stress Score

Score quantifying session training load based on intensity and duration.

U

Undulating Periodization

Intensity variation within the same week rather than by blocks.

V

Vertical Oscillation

Vertical bounce amplitude with each stride, ideally minimized.

VIVariability Index

Ratio between normalized and average power, indicates pacing consistency.

Vitamin D

Essential vitamin for bones, immunity, and muscle function, often deficient in runners.

VMAMaximal Aerobic Speed

Running speed at which oxygen consumption reaches its maximum.

VO2max

Maximum oxygen consumption, indicator of aerobic capacity.

Z5

Z

Zone 1

Active recovery - Very easy effort, effortless conversation.

Z1
Zone 2

Fundamental endurance - Sustained conversational pace.

Z2
Zone 3

Tempo - Intermediate 'gray' zone, moderately difficult.

Z3
Zone 4

Lactate threshold - Hard effort, limit of prolonged sustainability.

Z4
Zone 5

VO2max - Very intense effort, developing maximum aerobic power.

Z5
Zone 6

Anaerobic - Maximal effort, sprints and pure power.

Z6
